reading: The grid is cut into panels by full separator lines. One panel holds a template shape; the first panel of each panel-row holds a block in that row's colour. Every panel gets a copy of the template shape painted in its row's colour.
verb: stamp template into every panel, coloured by row

slots.template: the single non-square shape found in one panel (its colour is ignored)
slots.cells: every panel cut by the separators
slots.colour: the colour of the block in the first panel of the same panel-row
slots.rest: separators kept; old panel contents replaced

why: every panel equals the template mask filled with its row's key colour

reading: Panels come in left/right pairs separated by background stripes, each panel a solid colour with a shape drawn in another colour. The two shapes swap panels, and each shape is painted in the background colour of the panel it came from.

slots.pairs: the two panels sharing one panel-row
slots.subject: the non-background shape inside each panel
slots.placement: same relative position in the partner panel
slots.colour: the background colour of the source panel (so same-colour pairs end up blank)

why: each panel's shape cells equal its partner panel's input shape cells, coloured with the partner's background

reading: A large shape is built from k x k solid blocks on a 3x3 lattice, among scattered noise cells of a second colour. The output is that shape shrunk to 3x3 (one cell per block), painted in the noise colour.
verb: downscale shape and recolour with noise colour

slots.subject: the largest object (block-built shape), its box cut out
slots.colour: the colour of the scattered noise cells

why: output cell (i,j) is the noise colour exactly when block (i,j) of the large shape is filled

reading: Two-colour key bars at the left edge map shape colour a to b. Each shape gets its bounding box grown by one cell, and the background cells of that box reachable from outside the shape are filled with key(a); enclosed holes stay background.
verb: frame each shape with its key colour

slots.subject: each object right of the key column
slots.region: background cells inside the object's bounding box expanded by 1, excluding holes enclosed by the object
slots.colour: key(object colour) from the 2-colour bars at the left edge

why: every background cell in a shape's padded box and outside its holes becomes key(shape colour); nothing else changes

reading: The 4x4 input is scaled into a 4x4 grid of 4x4 blocks: each block is a copy of the input where the corresponding input cell is non-background, empty otherwise.
why: block (i,j) equals the input when input(i,j) is fg, else all background

reading: Two 2x2 squares, colours 1 and 2. The 1 square shoots a diagonal line of 1 from its top-left corner up-left to the border; the 2 square shoots a diagonal line of 2 from its bottom-right corner down-right to the border.
why: each square's ray runs diagonally (direction fixed per colour: 1 up-left, 2 down-right) until the grid border; squares unchanged

reading: Three equally spaced cells lie on a diagonal. Concentric square rings of that colour are drawn centred on the middle cell, ring radii being multiples of the cell spacing, out past the grid edge.

slots.centre: the middle of the three markers
slots.step: the diagonal spacing between consecutive markers
slots.extent: rings of radius step, 2*step, ... until outside the grid (clipped)

why: a cell is coloured exactly when its Chebyshev distance from the centre is a multiple of the step

reading: Three 5x5 panels are separated by columns of 6. The output is 5x5: columns 0-1 from the first panel, column 2 from the second panel, columns 3-4 from the third panel.

slots.panels: the three panels cut by the full 6 separator columns, in left-to-right order
slots.rule: output column j is panel k's column j, where k = left/middle/right third of the width (cols 0-1, 2, 3-4 for width 5)

why: each output column equals the same column of the panel assigned to that third of the width

reading: A single coloured cell shoots diagonal lines in all four diagonal directions until each reaches the grid border.
why: every cell on the marker's two diagonals has the marker colour, up to the border; nothing else changes

reading: A single-colour (8) blob is split into pieces: 2x2 squares become 1 and three-cell L pieces are coloured by orientation (missing top-left corner -> 2, missing bottom-left -> 3, missing top-right -> 4).
verb: decompose shape into tiles and colour by tile type

slots.subject: the 8-coloured cells
slots.pieces: a tiling of the blob by 2x2 squares and 3-cell L-trominoes inside 2x2 boxes
slots.colour: by piece shape: square 1; L missing top-left 2; missing bottom-left 3; missing top-right 4

why: every 8 cell is recoloured by the type of the tiling piece containing it; background unchanged
